[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on control of cell survival and proliferation decisions during tissue growth and differentiation. Two hubs stand out: the retinoblastoma protein RB1, which restrains the G1/S transition by holding E2F-dependent transcription in check and whose loss underlies retinoblastoma and many sporadic cancers, and BCL2L1, an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL2 family that guards mitochondrial outer membrane integrity and blocks cytochrome c release.

[untitled BTM module] The dominant theme here is chromatin-based control of gene expression coupled to ubiquitin-dependent protein regulation. Polycomb components BMI1 and EED, the histone chaperone ANP32E, the chromatin remodeller SMARCA5 and the histone-binding MORF4L2 together repress or reposition nucleosomes at developmental and proliferation genes, keeping stem and progenitor identity stable and restraining tumour suppressor loci such as the CDKN2A region.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on nuclear organisation and nucleocytoplasmic traffic: chromatin architecture, mRNA processing, ribosome biogenesis and export of cargo through the nuclear pore. CTCF and the cohesin subunit SMC1A together define chromatin loop boundaries and insulate promoters from inappropriate enhancers, which is how genome folding is translated into transcriptional output; ADNP and ATF1 act on transcription, the latter as a CREB-family factor responding to cAMP signalling.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on the braking and tuning of growth-factor signalling as it feeds into transcription, a control layer whose loss produces overgrowth, cancer and neurodevelopmental disease. Two GTPase-activating proteins, RASA2 for Ras and ACAP2 for an Arf-family GTPase, terminate signalling at the membrane, while MAP3K2 relays kinase input downstream and sorting nexins SNX13 and SNX14 govern endosomal trafficking and receptor fate.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the myeloid identity and activation program of monocytes and macrophages, the cells that patrol tissue for microbes and debris and set the tone of an inflammatory response. The transcription factor SPI1 (PU.1) specifies this lineage together with HHEX, while TLR4 senses bacterial lipopolysaccharide and PTAFR responds to platelet-activating factor, coupling through the Src-family kinase LYN, the phospholipase PLCB2 and the ITAM-bearing adaptor TYROBP (DAP12) to calcium mobilization and cytoskeletal change; DOK2 acts as a brake on this kinase signaling.
